flagged.location: ## Definition, clause (c) Outcome sets and exact values, final sentence
flagged.evidence: The Definition says the exact value λ is read through the singleton {λ} with probability μ^A_ρ({λ}), then says an exact value of a quantity with no eigenvalues is “an idealization outside the assignment.” Its own outcome law is defined on Borel sets of ℝ, and pthm-nrqm-observables-position-and-momentum-outcome-laws, clause (d), says atomlessness “does not remove ℝ from the law's Borel outcome space.” Zero probability for every singleton means no point masses; it does not remove real values from the outcome space or law. Lack of a normalizable eigenvector does not establish that stronger claim.

flagged.location: Postulate, clause (iv) Unsharp finite outcomes; Sources.references
flagged.evidence: Clause (iv) adopts probabilities tr(ρF_a) for finite families of bounded effects F_a with Σ_a F_a = I. The current Sources.references locate Teschl §2.1, Tong §§3.2–3.3, and Binney and Skinner §1.4. At those locations, Teschl discusses self-adjoint observables and expectation values, Tong presents Born probabilities from eigenstate expansions, and Binney and Skinner describes ideal measurements through expansion coefficients. These cited passages do not supply the finite-effects extension, and the source list gives no source for that clause. See [Teschl](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~gerald/ftp/book-schroe/schroe.pdf), [Tong](https://davidtong.org/pdfs/teaching/quantum-mechanics/qm.pdf), and [Binney and Skinner](https://www-thphys.physics.ox.ac.uk/people/JamesBinney/qb.pdf).
